subject: negative binomial in random effect multilevel model

messages.author: 48396400c8886bdc
messages.subject: negative binomial in random effect multilevel model
parts: I have heard that if there is a random effect in a multilevel model no need of negative binomial the Poisson would be enough even in case of over dispersion. Is that true?

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] negative binomial in random effect multilevel model
parts:
Instead of using negbinomial, you can use poisson with a random effect with as many levels as observations in the data. For instance:

dat$obs <- 1:nrow(dat)
fit <- brm(.... ~ ... + (1|obs), dat, family = poisson(), ...)
2017-10-26 18:50 GMT+02:00 Rolpio <rimap...@gmail.com>:
I have heard that if there is a random effect in a multilevel model no need of negative binomial the Poisson would be enough even in case of over dispersion. Is that true?

--

messages.author: 48396400c8886bdc
messages.subject: Re: negative binomial in random effect multilevel model
parts:
Ok wonderful,
so to be clear insteast of using the following code that defines the random effect at the second level (UPPERGEOG):

model <- brm(Y ~ relevel(SES1, ref= "Q1") + relevel(SES2, ref="Q1") + (1|UPPERGEOG)+ offset(log(EXP)), data = DATASET,family="poisson", control = list(max_treedepth = 35), autocor=cor_car(mat, type= ("escar")), prior=PriorBrFullLasso,warmup = 4000, iter =25000, chains= 6)


Should I use something like ? 

model <- brm(Y ~ 1|relevel(SES1, ref= "Q1") + 1|relevel(SES2, ref="Q1") + (1|UPPERGEOG)+ offset(log(EXP)), data = DATASET,family="poisson", control = list(max_treedepth = 35), autocor=cor_car(mat, type= ("escar")), prior=PriorBrFullLasso,warmup = 4000, iter =25000, chains= 6)

or should I create a specific DATASET$obs  <- 1:nrow(dat) and change my code in the following way ?

model <- brm(Y ~ + (1|obs), relevel(SES1, ref= "Q1") + relevel(SES2, ref="Q1") + (1|UPPERGEOG)+ offset(log(EXP)), data = DATASET,family="poisson", control = list(max_treedepth = 35), autocor=cor_car(mat, type= ("escar")), prior=PriorBrFullLasso,warmup = 4000, iter =25000, chains= 6)

Thank you for your help

On Thursday, October 26, 2017 at 10:50:00 AM UTC-6, Rolpio wrote:
I have heard that if there is a random effect in a multilevel model no need of negative binomial the Poisson would be enough even in case of over dispersion. Is that true?
